fields.title: Daemon restart must not lose in-flight runs: auto-resume on boot and on re-dispatch
fields.§h:Description:
Incident 2026-08-22: dispatchd restarted while three runs were in flight; all were force-failed by reconcileOnBoot (orchestrator.ts:3023) and one nearly-complete run (r-d236d7, session and worktree fully intact) was lost — re-dispatching its task via `dispatch run` spawned a FRESH run and the work had to be salvaged by hand-messaging the new agent.

All the machinery already exists: resumeRun (orchestrator.ts:3827) resumes with the same worktree, branch, sessionId, model, and claims — but its only caller is the human pressing Resume in the UI. Close three gaps:

1. reconcileOnBoot: after the existing survey settles, a force-failed run that is resumable — unreviewed, has a sessionId, worktree present, not already resumed — is auto-resumed through the resumeRun path instead of left dead. HAZARD: the orphaned agent process can survive the restart and keep committing (see stampOrphanWork, orchestrator.ts:1602) — never auto-resume while the orphan is provably alive or the branch is still gaining post-fail commits; defer and retry rather than fight the orphan for the worktree.
2. `dispatch run <taskId>`: when the task's most recent run is failed/interrupted-dirty, unreviewed, and resumable, resume it (resumedFrom chain) instead of spawning fresh; add --fresh to force a new run.
3. Expose resume directly: `dispatch run resume <runId>` calling the same daemon endpoint the UI uses.

Tests: extend packages/server/test/resilience.test.ts — restart mid-run with a fake executor, assert the run continues via a resumedFrom successor in the same worktree with no work lost; assert the orphan-alive case defers. Keep api.ts surface changes minimal — a live run currently claims that file.

1. Re-dispatch quiescence gate. `dispatchOrResume` now refuses (409, re-arming the sweep) when the run is boot-force-failed and nothing has yet watched its worktree settle. Only boot-force-failed runs owe that proof — a run that failed with its daemon alive has no orphan to race. The 409 says the run will resume on its own and points at fresh=true.

2. Evidence strengthened. `worktreeEvidence` now hashes the actual staged/unstaged diff CONTENT plus untracked size+mtime, and returns null for "cannot tell" — null never compares equal into a resume.
3. Task status. `resumeBlockReason` mirrors createRun's done/cancelled refusal (and refuses an unreadable task file).
4. Model consistency. A named model differing from the run's routes to a fresh run, same as executor. Only compared when the run's own model is known, so an older run recording none still resumes.
5. CLI sends `--executor` only when typed (getOptionValueSource); a default is not a request.
6. finishAutoResume re-checks blockReason after the awaited sample; the give-up note re-checks stopped+blockReason before claiming an orphan is still writing.
7. `dispatchOrResume` seam now used by api.ts createRun, EpicEngine auto-fill and warden dispatch_task.
Optional: stalling stub shared via test/orchestrator/helpers.ts; resilience test uses the real RunMeta; the 600ms wall-clock orphan test is now condition-polled; loop is delay-first.
Two things found while fixing, worth knowing:

- I introduced a real bug and caught it: `worktreeEvidence` ran git status + git diff concurrently, which lose the index.lock race in one worktree. That returns null = "cannot tell", so it would have quietly prevented EVERY resume. Now sequential.

- Sampling moved to strictly after each quiet window (no boot baseline). Beyond dropping the dead trailing wait, this stops boot firing a burst of git at every crashed worktree exactly when its orphan is most likely mid-commit — losing that race costs the ORPHAN a failed commit. It reproduced as a real aggregate-only failure in the pre-existing orphan-work test; aggregate now runs clean 3x.

fields.title: Fix loop false green: a review run killed mid-flight settles the loop as complete
fields.§h:Description:
Incident 2026-08-22: fix loops for t-7cc78a and t-48a2e5 were started, their round-0 review runs were killed by a dispatchd restart (state failed, zero findings recorded), and on the next start/advance both loops settled state=complete — lastReviewedSha had been stamped when the review was DISPATCHED (fixLoop.ts:405/659), so the dead review counted as done, and settle() (fixLoop.ts:734) saw zero open findings and declared the bar cleared. Neither branch was ever actually reviewed, and complete is sticky: stop + advance-with-baseSha does not reopen (step() returns unchanged for capped/complete, fixLoop.ts:292), so there is no API path out of the false green.

Fix: a review run that terminates without completing (failed / interrupted / force-failed by reconcileOnBoot) must not count as a completed review — either clear lastReviewedSha when the review run dies, or track the review's run id and require its state=finished before settle() may treat the round as reviewed. Also give complete a reopen path (ignite or advance with explicit baseSha reopens a settled loop) so a stuck state is recoverable without hand-editing fix-loops.jsonl. Tests: kill a review run mid-round with the fake executor, assert the loop re-reviews instead of settling; assert reopen works on a complete loop.

fields.title: Zero-turn resumed run finishes green: silent no-op reads as success
fields.§h:Description:
Incident 2026-08-22: run r-297e7b (a message --resume follow-up on t-48a2e5 carrying required review fixes) reached state=finished with turns=0, costUsd=0, no commits, and a transcript ending at the injected user message — the agent never executed a single turn, yet the run reads as a successful finish everywhere (runs list, fix loop, review surfaces). The requested fixes were silently not applied; only a manual diff caught it.

Likely area: the resume path in the executor/session handling — a resumed SDK session that terminates immediately (expired/terminal session id, or an SDK error mapped to a clean exit) is recorded as finished instead of failed. Fix: a run that finishes with zero turns (or no assistant output at all) after a resume must be state=failed with an explanatory error, not finished; consider the same guard for fresh runs. Test: resume with a stubbed executor that exits without turns, assert failed + error message. Related resilience cluster: t-050819 (restart auto-resume), t-350f21 (fix-loop false green) — all three are "dead thing reads as success" bugs.

dispatchd busy-loop: main thread pegs at 100% CPU, daemon goes unresponsive
fields.§h:Description:
Incident 2026-08-23 (~01:20 onward): the installed dispatchd (PID 58214, ~18h uptime, Dispatch.app build) pegged its MAIN thread at 100% CPU and stopped answering — CLI 'dispatch runs' hung past 120s, MCP task_comment/task_save hung to the 1800s idle timeout, process stayed alive. A 2s sample showed all 1515 samples in one synchronous call path on the main thread (stripped binary, no symbols — the shape is a hot loop, not slow I/O). Conditions: one execute run in flight (r-e0be91), a large run registry (~40 runs, several carrying multi-KB error strings), continuous board JSONL churn, a concurrent session active. SIGTERM did not exit it promptly; the app respawned a healthy daemon after kill.

Investigate candidate main-path hot loops: runs listing serialization (dispatch runs --json was already truncating on the large registry earlier the same day), fix-loop advance/stall rechecks, merge-queue refresh tick, survey scheduling re-entry. Repro lead: registry with many terminal runs carrying large error payloads + an active run. Include a watchdog (log a stack when the event loop stalls >N seconds) so the next spin is diagnosable. fields.title: Resume after daemon restart can silently start a fresh session, losing all conversation context
fields.§h:Description: Incident 2026-08-23: r-6dd770 (t-880ce2) was force-failed by a daemon restart mid-conversation (a design Q&A and a pending scope request were in its session). The user's 'ask again' message resumed it as r-ab889f — which started over from the base task prompt with NO memory of the conversation: the answered design question, the granted-in-principle scope request, and the binding amendments were all gone, silently. This is the third failure mode of the same seam: (1) t-ed735b zero-turn instant-finish, (2) lost pending approvals t-b2d83a, (3) this fresh-session-masquerading-as-resume. Root suspicion: the resume handle/session id persisted on a state line is lost or unusable across a daemon restart, and the fallback is a fresh session with resumedFrom still set — the run LOOKS like a resume in the registry but isn't one. A resume that cannot actually reattach its session must either fail loudly or explicitly re-inject the prior transcript, never silently start over. Related: t-050819 (merged), t-ed735b, t-b2d83a, t-bb4d21.

fields.title: Run-lifecycle resilience: no state may lie about whether work happened
fields.§h:Description: Groups the resilience bugs surfaced by the 2026-08-22/23 dogfooding marathon, all one family: a run/loop/request state that reads as success or simply vanishes when the underlying work did not happen. Members: t-350f21 (fix-loop settles complete after its review run died), t-ed735b (zero-turn resume finishes green), t-b2d83a (pending scope/approval requests lost on daemon restart), t-8f336a (resume silently starts a fresh session, losing conversation), t-bb4d21 (daemon main-thread busy-loop, unresponsive but alive). t-050819 (boot auto-resume, merged 2026-08-23) was the first of the family. Common thread: terminal-state bookkeeping is stamped optimistically (at dispatch/attempt time) rather than confirmed against what actually ran — fix the family with shared invariants and tests, not five point patches.

fields.title: Demo service leaks processes until fork fails; find and fix the reaper gap
fields.§h:Description:
On 2026-08-23 the dispatch-demo Railway service hit EAGAIN on every session create after ~12 days up: `cannot fork`, `cannot create async thread`, git spawn failures in doCreate (apps/demo/src/sessions.ts:130), and `daemon did not emit the expected stdout contract within timeout` — all process/thread exhaustion in the container. A `railway redeploy` cleared it.

Hypothesis: session teardown (idle reap after IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS / 30-min reset) leaves child processes behind — daemons, scripted-agent processes, or git subprocesses — accumulating until the container's pid/thread limit is hit.

To do:
- Audit apps/demo session teardown: does it kill the whole process tree (process group) or just the direct child? Zombies reaped?
- Add a counter/log of live children per reap cycle so exhaustion is visible before it bites.
- Consider a belt-and-braces periodic self-check (restart or refuse+alert when close to the limit).

fields.title: SQLite driver divergence: node:sqlite throws on >2^53 INTEGER reads, bun:sqlite silently rounds
fields.§h:Description:
Filed from the t-2b6de0 review. The driver seam in packages/core/src/sqliteDb.ts normalizes the one difference that reaches callers today (Statement.get() answering a miss with null vs undefined). This is the difference it deliberately does NOT normalize, recorded so it is a known debt rather than a surprise.

MEASURED, not theorized. Inserting 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1) into an INTEGER column and reading it back:

  node 24.3.0  -> THROWS: "Value is too large to be represented as a JavaScript number: 9007199254740993"
  bun 1.3.14   -> RETURNS 9007199254740992, silently. Off by one, no error.

WHY IT MATTERS. Both drivers read the SAME dispatch.db. The desktop app and dispatchd run under Bun; the CLI's declared runtime is Node (engines: node >=22). So a single value written once is a hard error on one half of the product and silent corruption on the other. That asymmetry is worse than either behaviour alone, because a bug report from a CLI user ("it throws") and one from a desktop user ("the number is wrong") would look unrelated.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT. Nothing in the schema can currently reach 2^53. The INTEGER columns are self_review, fix_loop and exercised (0/1 flags), findings.line and findings.round, and the per-run seq counter on evidence/mutations. lastInsertRowid could in principle, but only past ~9 quadrillion rows.

THE TRIGGER TO WATCH FOR. This stops being theoretical the moment someone adds a wide INTEGER column — an epoch-millis-times-something timestamp, a hash stored as an integer, a byte count, an externally-supplied id. The adapter's doc comment names this so whoever adds one has a chance of noticing.

THE FIX WHEN IT IS NEEDED. Read integers as BigInt on both drivers (bun: Statement.safeIntegers(true); node: Statement.setReadBigInts(true)) and narrow each back to a number in adaptDriver, throwing when the value is not exactly representable. That makes both runtimes behave like node:sqlite does now, which is the safe direction — loud rather than silently wrong. It was not done in t-2b6de0 because it costs a per-cell walk of every returned row on every read, and no column can currently trip it. Measure that cost against a realistic board (the dogfood .dispatch has ~200 tasks) before committing to it.

Alternative worth considering: a CHECK constraint or a write-side guard keeping wide integers out of the schema entirely, so the read side never has to care.

Now pnpm + `moon run` targets — deliberately `moon run` and not `moon ci`, since a merge-queue entry is already rebased so "affected" is the wrong question.

2. apps/demo/Dockerfile — same two commands. Build stage moves to node purely for pnpm (oven/bun ships no node/corepack); runtime stays bun. Builds only what the image serves via `--filter "@dispatch/sandbox..." --filter "@dispatch/desktop..."`, verified to resolve to the right 8 packages, which also drops astro/sharp-musl from an image that never serves the marketing page. NOT built end to end — docker's daemon is down here. Flagged in the commit.

3. AFFECTED WITHOUT DEPENDENTS — reproduced exactly: a commit touching only packages/core/src/ids.ts ran core's three targets and NOTHING in cli/client/mcp/desktop. Fixed with `--include-relations`, re-proved after: core fans out to cli/client/demo/desktop/mcp/server/web test+typecheck, while an apps/site-only commit still narrows to site alone. Note for anyone else looking: `--downstream deep` does NOT do this — it controls action-graph depth, not affected scope.
4. CATALOG IN NO INPUTS — measured 0 of 31 build/typecheck/test tasks. `moon task core:typecheck` now lists pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml among resolved inputs.

5. TOKENS STALE — fixed, and the obvious fix is a trap worth recording: giving tokens a `noop` build task does NOT work, because moon 2.3.3 does not fold a dependency task's hash into its dependents'. Measured: tokens:build re-ran while desktop:build and site:build stayed cached. Each consumer now lists `/packages/tokens/tokens.css` in its own build inputs; both rebuild.

6. PUBLISH GUARD — one correction to the finding: it fails CLOSED, not open (exit 1, not 0). But the effect is worse than it sounds — no release automation could publish at all, dying on "No tasks found" with no pointer to the cause. Both tasks are now runInCI 'always'; verified the guard runs and passes from a CI shell and still aborts on a pin mismatch.

7. HOOKS NOT INSTALLED BY pnpm install — confirmed on a fresh clone (hooksPath empty after install). `prepare: moon sync vcs-hooks` restores it; re-verified. Safe in Docker: `moon sync vcs-hooks` succeeds outside a git repo.
8. AGE-GATE WAIVERS — the four parent waivers removed; verified unnecessary (clean frozen install succeeds without them). Only the lockstep binary siblings remain.

9. root:format IN THE HOOK — removed. It ran `oxfmt .` over the whole worktree, so one file's commit rewrote unstaged edits and AGENTS.md's carto block, and in a shared checkout landed in another session's diff. lint-staged already formats the staged files.

10. SITE TYPECHECK VACUOUS — confirmed (0 files). Gave apps/site a tsconfig, mutation-tested. Extends the repo's tsconfig.options.json, not astro's `base`, because base leaves strictNullChecks off and oxlint's type-aware rules then hard-error on every newly covered file. .astro components remain unchecked and the config says so rather than pretending.

BIGGER FINDING THE REVIEW DIDN'T CATCH, same class as #10 and a regression I introduced: desktop:typecheck was checking ZERO files. apps/desktop/tsconfig.json is a solution file, so the inherited `tsgo --noEmit` resolved it and exited 0 — measured with a planted `const x: number = "s"`: tsgo reported nothing and passed, `tsc -b` reported TS2322. That is the whole desktop app, ~128 files, where main's per-package script had been running `tsc -b --noEmit` all along. Overridden to match, mutation-tested.

ALSO-LIST: all done. The one worth calling out is the `onlyBuiltDependencies` block — it was not just a dead duplicate, it was the WRONG KEY. pnpm 11 renamed it to `allowBuilds` and ignores the old name silently. The live block was the one `pnpm approve-builds` had appended at the bottom of the file. That also means my earlier ledger hazard blaming a stale node_modules cache for ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS was wrong; filed a correction (l-ec9734), since the wrong version was already in the ledger. Rest: setup action asks `pnpm store path` (the hardcoded Linux path cached nothing on release.yml's macOS jobs) and gained proto restore-keys; 71 duplicated glob lines collapsed into a `scan-excluded` fileGroup, verified behaviourally; wt.ts's parseOffset no longer reads a blank `DISPATCH_PORT_OFFSET=` as offset 0 (which is the MAIN CLONE's, so `wt clean` would have killed main's dev servers) and parseEnvFile uses a null-prototype accumulator; desktop's double build removed; load-worktree-env deleted; the "lifecycle hooks only" claim corrected in AGENTS.md.

NEW GUARD: scripts/check-ci-targets.ts, wired in as root:check-ci-targets, fails when ci.yml's target list and the root task graph disagree either way. That is the mechanism that left six lint lanes dark on main. Its own first version was vacuous — it anchored on the first literal "moon ci", which is in a comment, parsed an empty target set, printed "gates on all 0 root tasks" and passed all four mutations. Fixed to anchor on the `run: >-` block and to refuse to pass if either side is empty; re-mutated 4/4 caught. Recording that because it is exactly the failure the mutation instruction exists to catch, and I only found it by running the mutations.

VERIFICATION: 13/13 gates green (also green under --force, uncached). `moon run :build` 9/9, `moon run :typecheck` 16/16. Full `moon run :test`: every project green except server at 2182 pass / 3 fail — the same three pre-existing failures measured on an unmodified main checkout. One caution for the next person: `moon run :test --force` produces extra failures (a desktop:build "Rolldown failed to resolve @dispatch/core/browser", plus sandbox/cli flakes). Those are --force artifacts — it re-runs dependency builds so `tsdown --clean` can wipe core's dist under a concurrent consumer. sandbox and cli pass in isolation; the un-forced run is clean.

STILL OPEN, unchanged: the three server test failures need a product decision on whether inbox capture splits multi-line text; wt.ts's port offsets remain a reservation, not enforcement; GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw stays a recorded exception until @railway/cli ships a tar ^7 range. — agent:wsoule679/claude

Likely causes: cli:test/mcp:test lack dependsOn/inputs edges on the compiled CLI/daemon/mcp bin builds they spawn (local runs had warm dist), or CI env gaps (bun on PATH for compiled tests, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null trap per repo memory — retest suspects with that set). - 2026-09-03T19:45:39.191Z Root cause found — the missing edge, exactly as suspected in the description, plus the reason it looked like two different bugs.

THE EDGE. `.moon/tasks/bun-common.yml` defines the shared `test` task with `deps: ['^:build']`. In moon, `^:build` means "build my DEPENDENCY projects" — it never includes the project's own build. packages/cli's e2e tests spawn `node ../dist/cli.js` and packages/mcp's spawns `node ../dist/bin.js`; both artifacts are produced only by that project's OWN `build` task. So `cli:build`/`cli:test` and `mcp:build`/`mcp:test` sat in the graph as unordered siblings, free to run concurrently.

WHY IT PASSED LOCALLY AND NOT IN CI. Not env, not PATH, not GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL — all three suspects in the description are ruled out. Locally dist/ is always warm from an earlier build, so the missing edge is invisible. CI starts cold.
PROOF IT IS A RACE, NOT JUST A MISSING BINARY — from the run-33796780684 timestamps:
cli:test  started 19:31:46.3 | cli:build started 19:31:48.2  (build began 2s AFTER the test)
mcp:test  started 19:31:24.5 | mcp:build finished 19:31:25.7 (test spawned the bin mid-build)

That also explains the two different failure shapes. cli died with a clean `Cannot find module .../packages/cli/dist/cli.js` (file simply absent). mcp instead hung to its 15s timeout because tsdown builds with `--clean`: the binary was being deleted and rewritten underneath a spawn that had already started, so the process came up but never answered the initialize handshake.

The race is also why CI reported 4 cli failures while a cold local run reports 5 — cli:build completed at 19:31:48.7, partway through cli:test's 8.5s run, so the test files scheduled after that instant found dist/cli.js present and passed. This would have been intermittent across reruns, not reliably red.

FIX. `test: deps: ['build']` in packages/cli/moon.yml and packages/mcp/moon.yml. moon merges rather than replaces inherited deps, so `^:build` is retained (verified: cli:test now depends on cli:build + mcp:build + core:build). This is not a new pattern — apps/site and apps/desktop already carry this exact override with a comment explaining the same trap; cli and mcp were simply missed in the migration.
VERIFIED. Deleted every packages/*/dist and reran: cli:test 203 pass / 0 fail, mcp:test 116 pass / 0 fail. Previously 5 fail plus the 15s timeout.
The 3 server failures (filterGroupsToLocalItems, POST /api/inbox, GET /api/linear/status) are unchanged and remain t-9c2129's. — agent:wsoule679/claude
- 2026-09-03T21:07:28.238Z BLOCKER — a fourth pre-existing CI failure the description does not account for, left unfixed because the scope request was denied on timeout.

log 6144: root:format-check | AGENTS.md (126ms)
log 6146: root:format-check | Format issues found in above 1 files.

The carto-generated `<!-- CARTO:AUTO -->` block has never been oxfmt-clean: a missing blank line after the START marker, an unwrapped `**High impact:**` line, an unaligned markdown table, and a missing blank line before the END marker. It is committed in a shape the repo's own formatter rejects.
THE FIX, verified working, for whoever picks it up (one hand edit, then the formatter does the rest):
1. In AGENTS.md, insert a blank line between `- 📄 tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` and `**High impact:**`.
2. Run `moon run root:format`.
3. `moon run root:format-check` then passes, and oxfmt is idempotent on the result.

Step 1 is load-bearing and is why `moon run root:format` alone is not the answer: without it oxfmt folds the `**High impact:** ...` paragraph INTO the preceding `- tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` list item, silently turning a standalone paragraph into list-item text. That is content damage, which is presumably why previous sessions kept reverting the file (there is a standing note that `format` rewrites AGENTS.md and to `git checkout` it before staging) — the revert habit is what has kept this failure alive on main.
I did NOT reach for an oxfmt exclusion for the generated block. Scoping a rule off in config is not how this repo fixes findings, and the block is committed source like anything else.

NOT DONE HERE because AGENTS.md is outside this task's declared writes and `request_scope` returned denied ("No one decided in time"), whose documented handling is to stay inside the fence and report. Reverted to main's content; my diff is 4 files, none of them AGENTS.md.

fields.title: Astro RCE advisory: apps/site pins 5.18.2, fix requires >= 7.2.8
fields.§h:Description:
GHSA-26w7-cxv4-gfx2 — "Astro: Remote code execution through AVIF image optimization", severity critical, vulnerable <7.2.8, patched >=7.2.8. The catalog pins astro 5.18.2 (pnpm-workspace.yaml:142), so root:audit (scripts/audit-gate.ts, `pnpm audit --audit-level critical`) fails on every push and main's CI stays red. First seen 2026-09-08 in CI run 34284836878; the advisory is new, not a regression from any commit.

\## Scope of the risk

The finding is dev: true on apps__site>astro — a build-time dependency of the marketing site. The desktop release artifact does not contain it: .github/workflows/release.yml builds only apps/desktop (Tauri app + bun-compiled sidecars). The exposure is the site's own build, which runs on trusted inputs, plus whatever serves the built output (Railway, see `bun run deploy` in apps/site).

\## Why this is not a one-line bump

There is no patched 5.x or 6.x: the advisory's patched range starts at 7.2.8, so this is a two-major upgrade of the site's framework. Expect breaking changes in astro's config, content collections, and image handling.

\## Blocked locally

pnpm cannot run on this machine at all — every invocation fails with ERR_PNPM_PNPM_ENGINE_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIABLE ("Cannot verify the identity of the @pnpm/exe.darwin-x64 native binary: it is missing from pnpm-lock.yaml"). The lockfile cannot be updated until that is resolved, so this task needs a working pnpm first.

\## Done when

- The catalog pins astro >= 7.2.8 and the lockfile is regenerated.
- `moonx site:build` succeeds and `moonx site:test` passes.
- The rendered site is checked by a human (agent shells cannot drive Playwright here).
- `moon run root:audit` exits clean.

fields.title: Site redesign: rebuild the marketing page in the codebahn.net mould
fields.§h:Description:
Wyat, 2026-09-08: "we are updating the website to be like this: https://codebahn.net/". Direction captured before the work starts; the shape below is from reading that site, not a spec Wyat wrote.

\## What codebahn.net does

Numbered sections (01-05) give the page a spine: Why, Performance, Migration, Pricing, Founder quote. Restraint is the whole aesthetic — light mode with a dark toggle, near-monochrome with one accent, no gradients, cards with thin borders, generous vertical rhythm (80-120px between sections), product screenshots shown unframed rather than in device mockups. Copy is short, direct and a little irreverent ("GitHub is overkill for most developers", "Migration sounds like a project. It is not"), and it leads with concrete numbers (128ms average tool call, 3.3x faster) instead of adjectives. Two CTAs everywhere: Get started, and a live demo. Footer is five columns including explicit "vs GitHub / vs GitLab / vs self-hosting" comparisons.

\## Where our site is now

apps/site is 12 files, ~400 lines of Astro across nine components: Nav, Hero, LeadShot, WhatYouGet, WhyBoard, LiveDemo, OpenSource (held back behind the e-c25f9c publication flag), Faq, Footer. One page, empty astro config, no integrations. It runs on astro 7.2.10 as of today.

\## Open questions for Wyat, before building

- Which of codebahn's sections map onto Dispatch: is there a pricing tier story yet, and do we want the numbered 01-05 spine?
- What are our concrete numbers? Codebahn's credibility comes from measured claims; ours would need real ones (runs landed, review latency, cost per task) rather than invented ones.
- Founder-voice section: keep, or not?
- Does the OpenSource section come back on with this redesign, given the publish epic?
- Light-first with a dark toggle, or stay as-is?

\## Constraints

- Deploys to Railway via `bun run deploy` from apps/site (local astro build, image ships prebuilt dist).
- Playwright cannot run in an agent shell here, so the visual pass is Wyat's.

fields.title: Root-cause the Bun.spawnSync kevent spin; move the daemon's remaining sync git off spawnSync
fields.§h:Description:
t-bb4d21 landed on epic/e-ac6705 as d077c536 (run r-34f186, 189 turns). Verification passed it, but four things it explicitly did not settle are worth carrying forward rather than losing in a closed task.

\## 1. The titled symptom is still unexplained

The run established, with a mutation-proof test (packages/server/test/blockingGit.test.ts:57, against a `trap "" TERM` child), that BoardSyncer ran `git pull --rebase`/`git push` over ssh through `Bun.spawnSync` on the event loop, and that Bun's spawnSync timeout is advisory: it sends SIGTERM once and then waits forever. That explains a daemon that is alive but unresponsive and does not exit on SIGTERM. It does NOT explain the 100% CPU the incident reported, and the agent said so plainly: "no JS infinite loop exists in the daemon", and the honest description is "main thread blocked in synchronous git", not a busy loop. So the original incident may have a second, still-unknown cause. If it recurs, sample the main thread again and compare against the now-instrumented watchdog output before assuming this fix covered it.

\## 2. The watchdog is unproven where it matters

`watchdogWorker.ts` runs as a worker thread and is a second compile entrypoint in apps/desktop/scripts/build-sidecars.ts. It was verified to resolve in a standalone `bun build --compile` probe, never against a real packaged Dispatch.app sidecar. Nothing in CI guards that `extraEntries` line, so a future edit can silently ship a daemon whose watchdog never loads — the failure is invisible until an incident it was supposed to instrument. Add a check that the compiled sidecar actually starts its watchdog.

\## 3. Leaked watchdogs make the test suite lie

Running the server suite emits `event loop stalled 16s in: git config user.name` lines from watchdogs that outlive their tests. They are false, and they will train readers to ignore the one that is real. Tear the watchdog down with the server that started it.

\## 4. Merge hazard when e-ac6705 lands into main

Both this branch and main (c673eaa0) independently fixed `removeDaemonFile` deleting a daemon file it no longer owned, and converged on the same `ownerPid` design — so git will conflict there. Keep main's version: it additionally tolerates an unparsable file (try/catch around the parse) where the branch's `readDaemonFile` would throw during shutdown.

Also weigh whether the CLI's 60s request ceiling is right for a slow local git route; it is a judgment call the run flagged itself.

fields.title: Epic PR poller missed two merged landing PRs the installed daemon had recorded
fields.§h:Description:
2026-09-11: epic landing PRs #28 (e-ac6705) and #29 (e-6cfcc7) were opened through POST /api/epics/:id/land and both were recorded in the daemon's epic-PR registry (~/.dispatch/runs/<key>/epic-prs.json held both URLs). Both PRs were merged on GitHub (892df5ed and 434d4b9f on main). Ten-plus minutes later neither epic had been marked landed and both URLs were still in the registry, so `pollEpicPrsOnce` never saw state MERGED for them. The same daemon process (pid 6306, started 2026-09-07) had marked e-ad1978 landed within eight seconds of PR #27 merging two days earlier. The epics were set to landed by hand.

\## What was ruled out from outside the process

- `gh pr view <url> --json state` returns MERGED for both from a shell, with and without GITHUB_TOKEN in the environment.
- The daemon's environment has no GITHUB_TOKEN, and its PATH resolves `gh` at /usr/local/bin.
- The poll loop is a self-rearming setTimeout chain whose tick catches and logs errors, so a thrown error should not stop it — but the daemon's log file under ~/.dispatch/logs carried only its two startup lines, so wherever console.error goes for an app-spawned daemon, it was not inspectable.

\## What to establish

1. Whether the loop was still running (an in-process counter or a `lastPolledAt` in health would answer this in future; today there is no way to tell).
2. Whether `this.run(['gh','pr','view',…])` was returning `ok: false` — that path is a silent `continue`, so a gh that starts failing (auth expiry, rate limit, a version prompt on stdout) hides forever. At minimum log once per URL when a view fails, with stderr.
3. Whether the two-day-old installed build differs from main's pr.ts in a way that explains it.

\## Done when

- The poller exposes when it last ran and last succeeded (health `problems` or a field), so a stalled poll is visible.
- A failed `gh pr view` is logged with its stderr rather than swallowed.
- A test covers a registry entry whose view fails N times and then succeeds.

fields.title: branchLayout: pure git-graph layout for one milestone's tasks
fields.§h:Description:
Add apps/desktop/src/lib/branchLayout.ts, a pure function over DagTask[] (reuse the DagTask shape and dagTaskFromDoc from dagLayout.ts) that produces a vertical git-log layout for one milestone's children: (1) a topological row order, blockers before dependents, deterministic by (created, id) like dagLayout's computeLayers and core's computeStack, using only real edges (blockedBy ids inside the set, non-self) and tolerant of cycles (leftovers appended in (created, id) order, never dropped); (2) the critical path, the longest chain measured over unfinished tasks (isDoneStatus from @dispatch/core/browser counts as finished), with a deterministic tie-break; (3) a lane per row where lane 0 is the critical path and side branches take the lowest free lane, released when their last dependent is placed; (4) edge segments {from, to, fromLane, toLane, fromRow, toRow} for the gutter to draw; (5) laneCount and a path summary {remaining, total, nextId} where nextId is the first unfinished path task whose blockers are all done. A set with no real edges lays out as a single trunk. Include a doc comment explaining what the layout is and why it exists.

Acceptance criteria:

- branchLayout(tasks) returns rows (id, lane, row index, onPath flag), edges, laneCount, path (ordered ids) and pathSummary
- Blockers always precede dependents in row order; identical input yields byte-identical output across calls
- Critical path excludes done tasks and is the longest remaining chain; a fully-landed milestone yields an empty path and remaining 0
- Lane assignment never gives two overlapping active branches the same lane; a diamond (A -> B, A -> C, B and C -> D) yields two lanes
- A cycle among children does not throw and every task still gets a row
- branchLayout.test.ts covers: empty set, no-edges trunk, linear chain, diamond, two independent chains, done tasks off the path, cycle tolerance

fields.title: Cut agent token cost
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
Agent sessions are dominated by cache reads, not output. Measured on the agent-communication worktree (2026-09-23 → 2026-10-06, ~1,400 transcripts): ~\$10.9k at API list prices; 15.2B cache-read tokens = ~70% of cost; output ~\$110.

- Subagents made 96% of cache reads (14.6B vs 1.1B for main sessions).
- The worst agents ran 2,000–2,500 turns at ~480k average context.
- 65% of reads happened on turns above 200k context; 32% above 400k.

Every turn re-reads the whole context, so cost ≈ context size × turns. These tasks cap context, move routine work to cheaper models, keep bulky output and CI polling out of the model, and make the cost visible per run. Order: measurement (visibility) first so the other changes can be judged on cost per landed task.

fields.title: Show where a run's money went: context size and subagent share
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
Usage already records the four token kinds per run (orchestrator/usage.ts) and subagentRequests, but nothing explains a costly run.

- Record peak and average context per turn, and turns, per run and per subagent.
- Split cache reads between the run's own turns and its subagents'.
- Run view: one line like "72% of cost was re-reading a 450k context; 3 subagents ran 2,000+ turns".
- Dashboard: cost per landed task, so the other tasks in this epic can be judged.

Do this first: it measures the rest.

fields.title: Hand off to a fresh session when a run's context passes a threshold
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
65% of cache reads in the measured window happened on turns above 200k context. When a run's context crosses a configurable threshold (default ~200k), ask the agent for a short handoff note (done / left / open questions / files touched), store it on the task, and continue in a new session seeded from the task spec, the note and the current diff.

Builds on durable sessions and run resume. Config: a per-executor threshold, off by default until measured. Acceptance: a long run crosses the threshold, hands off, and lands; usage shows the drop in average context.

fields.title: Subagent model setting: let a run's helpers use a cheaper model
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
Subagents made 96% of cache reads. Today a dispatched run's own subagents inherit the run's model. Add a subagent role next to the existing executors.<name>.models roles and pass it to Claude Code's subagent-model setting, so a run can stay on Opus while its helpers run on Sonnet (cache reads $0.30/M vs $0.50/M).

Acceptance: config validates the role; a run's subagent usage shows up under the configured model in byModel.

fields.title: Wake a run only on red CI with the failing job's log tail; tell runs not to watch checks
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description: Agents that loop on gh pr checks --watch pay a full context re-read per check, at 400k+ context. Check what pr.ts and mergeQueue already wait on. Then make runs stop at review, let Dispatch wait for CI outside the model, and wake an agent only on red, handing it only the failing job's log tail.

fields.title: Spill large command output to files; the agent gets a tail and the path
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description: Test and CI logs land in the context and are re-read on every later turn. Dispatch sets up its runs, so add a hook that writes any command output over a few thousand tokens to a file under the run's scratch dir and returns the last ~50 lines plus the path. Measure the change with the run cost breakdown task.

fields.title: Map task labels/kind to a model role, on top of the judged tier
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description: Mechanical work (dependency bumps, lint fixes, rebases, release chores) defaults to Sonnet; design and debugging stay on Opus. A label or kind maps to a model role, overridable per task. Depends on the subagent model setting landing first.

fields.title: Overseer tool: discard a finished run
fields.§h:Description:
The overseer can't close out finished runs. `cancel_run` (packages/server/src/orchestrator/overseerTools.ts:1037) only stops live runs and throws `run already finished` for anything else. Failed or interrupted runs nobody has reviewed stay in "waiting on you" forever, even after their task has landed. Example: 8 failed runs on the landed tasks t-4b72c5 and t-9ac0f5.

Add a mutating overseer tool, `discard_run`, that does what the app's discard does: `ctx.orchestrator.review(runId, 'discard')`, the same path as POST /api/runs/:id/review with `action: 'discard'` (packages/server/src/api.ts `reviewRun`).

Done looks like:
- `discard_run({ runId })` is an `OverseerMutatingTool`. Like every other mutating tool, it queues an approval card and does not act when called.
- `describe()` rejects unknown runs and live runs. A live run should be cancelled with `cancel_run` first. `describe()` also rejects runs already merged or discarded, or sitting in the merge queue. The card text names the run, the task title and the run's state (failed / interrupted-dirty, etc.).
- The card text warns when the worktree has uncommitted changes (interrupted-dirty), because discarding drops them with no undo.
- The tool is registered alongside cancel_run and listed in the overseer's system-prompt tool summary.
- Tests in packages/server/test cover: discarding a failed run, rejecting live, merged and queued runs, and an unknown id.
- Optional: accept `runIds: string[]` so a cleanup like the 8 above is one card, not eight.

Verify: `moon run root:format`, `moon run root:lint`, `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx server:test`.

fields.title: Memory hygiene: supersede, retire task-scoped notes, flag near-duplicates, show store health
fields.§h:Description:
Memory already guards against exact-duplicate text (content hash), too many writes (rate limits), a pile-up of pending proposals (cap plus TTL) and idle entries (decay: stale after 60 days, expired after 180; packages/memory/src/decay.ts). Nothing tidies the *content* itself. Seen in the current store:
- Near-duplicates: #2QVT8DHP and #NJ8NX0PJ record the same migration-scope decision, written 8 minutes apart.
- Corrections don't retire what they correct: #RY9DF7NY says it CORRECTS #YPF25THH, and both are still active. Decay is by last use, so a superseded entry that still gets recalled never goes stale.
- Notes that only mattered for one task outlive it: #E238CS1A ("Scope extended … for review fixes 9 and 10").
- Expired entries are only ever marked expired, never deleted, and no view shows how big the store is.

Done looks like:
1. **Supersede.** A memory write can name `supersedes: <id>`. On accept, the old entry is retired, with a revision whose cause is 'superseded'. memory_save and the MCP tool expose the field.
2. **Retire task-scoped notes.** An entry whose refs point only at a single task (and is not pinned, not a human constraint, and not kind hazard or convention) is proposed for retirement when that task lands. The proposal goes through the existing memory gate cards; nothing is deleted silently.
3. **Near-duplicate candidates.** The decay sweep flags pairs in the same scope with highly similar normalized titles or bodies (an FTS5 or trigram similarity threshold) as merge candidates. A human merges or dismisses them; no automatic merge.
4. **Health.** Settings → Memory shows counts of active, stale and expired entries, open proposals and merge candidates per scope, with a Review list. Expired entries older than a configurable `memory.purgeAfterDays` (default 365) are deleted outright, with their revisions kept in receipts.
5. Tests in packages/memory and packages/server/test/memory cover supersede, task-landed retirement proposals, candidate detection and purge.

Verify: `moon run root:format`, `moon run root:lint`, `moonx memory:typecheck`, `moonx memory:test`, `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx server:test`, and `moonx desktop:test` for the Settings view.

fields.title: Overseer: auto-apply low-risk actions by policy instead of queueing a card
fields.§h:Description:
Today every call to one of the overseer's mutating tools queues an approval card (packages/server/src/orchestrator/overseer.ts `callTool`: "a mutating tool only queues"), whatever the permission mode. Even a create_task or update_task the human would always approve costs them a click. The built-in tool gate already has an auto path (`authorizeTool`: acceptEdits plus grants); mutating overseer tools have none.

Done looks like:
- A project setting, `overseer.autoApply`, lists the tool names that apply immediately instead of queueing. It goes in config.yml next to `policy`. Read it through a helper like `projectPolicy()`, and make it editable in Settings, gated as an operator-only key in `operatorOnlyKeys` because it widens what an agent may do.
- The default is empty (today's behavior). A suggested preset for the Settings toggle covers create_task, update_task, create_plan and message_run.
- Some tools can never be auto-applied, and config validation rejects them with a warning: send_as_you (speaks as the human), dispatch_task (spends money), queue_merge (lands code), and approve_run / deny_run (answer gates on the human's behalf). Also cancel_run and discard_run (t-289065), which destroy in-flight work.
- An auto-applied action still goes through `registry.applyAction` and still writes the same action record, transcript line and receipt as an approved card, marked `decidedBy: policy`. The tool result says it was applied, not queued, so the model reports it as done.
- If `describe()` throws, or applying fails, the result is the same isError as today. Nothing falls through to a silent no-op.
- Tests in packages/server/test cover: a listed tool applies without a card; an unlisted one queues; a never-auto tool listed in config is rejected at load and still queues.

Verify: `moon run root:format`, `moon run root:lint`, `moonx core:typecheck`, `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx server:test`, `moonx desktop:test`.

fields.title: Approve all for overseer action cards, and "allow for this conversation" for safe mutating tools
fields.§h:Description:
When the overseer queues several cards in one turn (54 task edits in one cleanup this session), the human has to answer each card on its own. Needs you already has an "Approve all" button for lessons (apps/desktop/src/components/tasks/NeedsYouBlock.tsx `approveAll`), but not for overseer action cards. Also, the "Allow for this conversation" grants (overseerGrants.ts, `decideApproval`) cover only the built-in tools, never the mutating overseer tools.

Done looks like:
- Needs you and the Overseer transcript group a turn's pending overseer actions into one block with **Approve all** and **Deny all**. Each card stays individually decidable. Approve all applies them in queue order and reports each failure on its own card without stopping the rest.
- A card for a tool on the auto-apply allow-list from the sibling task (never send_as_you, dispatch_task, queue_merge, approve_run/deny_run, cancel_run or discard_run) offers "Allow <tool> for this conversation". This adds a GrantStore entry keyed by tool name, with the same 4-hour TTL and the same end on session rollover. Until the grant expires, later calls of that tool in this conversation apply immediately, recorded as `decidedBy: grant`.
- Server: a batch-decide endpoint, or a client loop over the existing confirm route, whichever keeps receipts per action. Tests cover the batch order and partial failure, grant expiry and the excluded tools.

Verify: `moon run root:format`, `moon run root:lint`, `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx server:test`, `moonx desktop:typecheck`, `moonx desktop:test`.

fields.title: Land button says exactly where the work went; no local-only land path when a remote exists
fields.§h:Description:
On 2026-10-06, run r-261399 (t-289065) was "landed". Its review-merge happened at reviewedAt 20:11:53, and it never appears in the merge queue's history. The result was a squash commit on the LOCAL main (a1a7606a) that was never pushed, while origin moved 53 commits ahead and shipped v0.39.0 and v0.39.1 without it. The human reasonably believed "Land" meant shipped. t-f00b6d makes the queue land on origin. This task makes every path and every label agree with that.

Done looks like:
- **One path.** `Orchestrator.review(runId, 'merge')` (api.ts `reviewRun`) and any other direct-merge path go through the same origin-first landing as the queue whenever the project has a remote. With a remote, there is no code path that squash-merges into local main alone.
- **Honest labels.** Wherever the app says Land or Landed (task status, run detail, Needs you, the landing feed), it names the destination: "Land on origin/main" before, and "Landed on origin/main · <sha>" with a GitHub link after. A no-remote project says "Land on local main" and "Landed locally (no remote)".
- **No silent split-brain.** If a landing reaches local main but not origin (a push failed, or the network is down), the run and task show "Merged locally — not on GitHub yet", with a one-click retry, and appear in Needs you. They are never shown as plain "landed".
- **Released?** The landed row shows whether the commit is in the latest release tag ("in v0.39.1" or "not released yet"), so "did it deploy" has an answer in the app.
- Tests cover the review-merge path with a remote (lands on origin), the no-remote fallback, and the push-failed state reaching Needs you.

Verify: `moon run root:format`, `moon run root:lint`, `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx server:test`, `moonx desktop:typecheck`, `moonx desktop:test`.

fields.title: Overseer chat: edit or remove a queued message before it goes out
fields.§h:Description:
\## Problem
While an Overseer turn is running, anything the human sends is queued on the conversation record (`OverseerRecord.queued`, appended in `Overseer.sendMessage`, packages/server/src/orchestrator/overseer.ts ~L464) and sent as one turn by `sendQueued` when the turn ends. The chat renders these as "Queued · goes out when this turn ends" (apps/desktop/src/components/chat/OverseerChat.tsx ~L568, testid `overseer-queued`), but there is no way to fix a typo, rewrite, or drop a queued line: it goes out exactly as typed.

\## Done looks like
- Each queued message in OverseerChat has Edit and Remove affordances. Edit swaps the bubble for an inline textarea (Enter/Save commits, Esc cancels); Remove deletes it.
- Server: routes to edit and delete one queued entry, e.g. `PATCH /api/overseer/:id/queued/:index` (or a stable per-entry id, preferred — add an `id` to each queued entry so an edit can't hit the wrong line if the queue shifts) and `DELETE` for the same. Both go through the same speaker/principal check as `POST /api/overseer/:id/message`, refuse when the bus is revoked like sendMessage does, and broadcast the record change so other open clients update.
- Race: if the turn ends and `sendQueued` has already sent the queue, an edit/delete gets a clear 409 ("already sent") and the UI says so instead of silently doing nothing. Emptying the queue entirely means nothing is sent when the turn ends.
- Edits never reach the agent before the turn ends — only the final text is sent.
- Client API methods in packages/client to match.

\## Tests
- Server: edit/delete a queued entry, then end the turn and assert only the edited text is sent; delete-all sends nothing; edit after send → 409; unknown entry id → 404.
- Desktop: component test for edit (save + cancel) and remove on a queued bubble, using OverseerChat.test.tsx's existing fakes.

fields.title: Project switcher lists run worktrees and scratch dirs as projects
fields.§h:Description:
The desktop project switcher shows a pile of "projects" that aren't real ones.

\## Why (likely)
`App.tsx` (~L347) builds the list by merging two sources:
1. The registry (`~/.dispatch/projects.json`, `listRegisteredProjects`). It's clean: 5 entries.
2. "Discovered" projects: `listProjects()` → `queries::list_projects` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/db/queries.rs:321`), meaning every cwd the session index has seen, kept if `has_dispatch(path)` is true (`sidecar.rs:971`, just checks that `<path>/.dispatch` is a directory).

`.dispatch/` is committed (team.yml etc.), so every run worktree under `~/.dispatch/worktrees/<hash>/r-xxxxxx` passes that check as soon as an agent session runs there. Paths that were deleted may also hang around in the session DB. Scratch checkouts like `.agents/ignore/storefront` can get in the same way.

\## Done when
- Discovered entries leave out paths under the dispatch worktrees root (`~/.dispatch/worktrees`) and any path that is a linked git worktree (where `.git` is a file, not a dir). Running `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` vs `--git-dir` works for this too.
- Paths that no longer exist on disk are left out.
- The existing registry-first ordering and dedupe stay as they are. A registered project always shows, even when it would otherwise be filtered out.
- Do the filtering in Rust (in or next to `list_projects`/`has_dispatch`) so the frontend doesn't fan out more checks. Add a unit test that covers a worktree path, a missing path, and a real repo.
- Optional: think about whether discovery should only run once the registry is empty, or whether to drop it now that the registry exists. Note what you decide.

First confirm the theory by printing the discovered list on this machine.

fields.title: Remove completed agent entries from the left sidebar
fields.§h:Description:
The desktop left sidebar keeps showing agent entries after they have finished. Once an agent completes, its entry should drop out of the sidebar. In-progress items and items that still need the human should stay.

Where to look:
- `apps/desktop/src/components/shell/DraftTray.tsx`: the Drafts tray maps `ready` items to TaskRow's `done` state and renders them, so finished entries stay listed. This is the most likely source.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx` (~line 357): `draftCount` already counts only running, ready or has-questions drafts. Make sure the count and the tray agree after the change.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/liveRail.ts` / `LiveRail.tsx`: the Live agents section already filters with `isTerminalRunState`. Confirm nothing terminal leaks through, for example a group whose runs have all finished.

Done when:

- Running entries, and entries with open questions or waiting on approval, still show.
- Completed work can still be reached from its full page (All agents, Drafts view).

fields.title: Overseer: risk-tiered actions so fewer things need approval
fields.§h:Description:
Today every mutating overseer tool call is queued as an approval card (`callTool` in `packages/server/src/orchestrator/overseer.ts`, ~line 1011). Creating a task gets the same card as cancelling a run, so the human approves far too often. Built-in tools already have tiers (`authorizeTool`: the floor.ts hold, `acceptEdits`, per-conversation grants). Give overseer actions the same treatment.

\## Tiers
- **Low: auto-run, no card.** create_task, update_task, create_plan, message_run. Runs immediately. The tool result tells the model it is DONE, not queued, so the overseer reports it as done.
- **Medium: ask once per conversation.** dispatch_task, approve_run/deny_run, queue_merge/dequeue_merge. The first call shows a card with "Allow for this conversation" (reuse the grants mechanism that built-in tools use, keyed by tool name). After that grant, later calls of that tool in the same conversation auto-run.
- **High: always ask.** cancel_run, discarding a run, send_as_you. No grant can skip these.
- Add a project setting `overseer.autonomy: cautious | balanced | trusting` (default `balanced` = the tiers above). `cautious` = today's behaviour, everything asks. `trusting` = medium tier also auto-runs. The high tier always asks in every mode.

\## Receipts for auto-run actions
- Every auto-run action posts a receipt in the Overseer chat: what was done, plus a link that opens the task in Tasks.
- For update_task, the receipt (or the task's history view it links to) shows the diff of what changed: fields before → after (title, description, priority, parent, blockedBy).
- Auto-run actions are still written to the ledger as they are now, marked as auto-approved with the tier, so they can be audited.

\## Batching
- When one overseer turn queues several actions that still need approval, show them on one card with "Approve all", plus per-item approve/deny. This replaces one card per action, here and in Needs you on Tasks.

\## Done when
- Low-tier tools run without a card and leave a chat receipt linking to the task. update_task receipts show the diff.
- Medium-tier tools ask once and then honour the per-conversation grant. High-tier tools always ask.
- The `overseer.autonomy` setting works for all three values and is documented.
- Several pending actions from one turn appear as a single batched card.
- The overseer system prompt / QUEUED_NOTE wording is updated so the model says "done" for auto-run actions and "queued" only for ones that are actually queued.
- Tests cover the tier routing, grants, the setting, and batching. `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx server:test`, `moonx desktop:typecheck`, `moonx desktop:test`, `moon run root:format` and `moon run root:lint` pass.

fields.title: Run chat: keep one persistent conversation per task instead of a new run per message
fields.§h:Description:
\## Problem
Each message the human sends in a run's chat makes a brand-new run. If the run has already ended, the composer calls `sendMessage(runId, text, { resume: true })` (`packages/server/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts` ~L1659). That goes to `requestChanges()`, which forks a NEW RunMeta into the same worktree. Wakes do the same thing (`wakeTask` / `wakeRun`, ~L2416–2470). So:
- the chat breaks up into many run chats, and the conversation doesn't persist in one place;
- the new run's chat often never starts: it opens empty or stuck instead of streaming the agent's reply.

\## Done looks like
1. **Persistent chat:** a task's run chat reads as one continuous conversation. A follow-up message carries on the same thread. It does not open a separate run chat. Either (a) reuse the same run record and session (go back from ended to running and append to its transcript), or (b) keep the forked runs but show them as one chained thread in the desktop UI, with the history of earlier runs in the chain shown inline. Pick the one that fits the registry/ledger model best, and give the reason in the PR.
2. **New chats start:** after a follow-up, the agent's reply streams into the chat the human is looking at, with no manual refresh or navigation. Find out why the forked run's chat doesn't start today (event subscription keyed on the old run id? session resume failing? UI not following the new run id?) and fix it.
3. Existing guarantees still hold: one live run per task, double-Enter dedupe (409), refusing reviewed/discarded runs, open-PR request-changes keeps updating the same branch, and FixLoop's automatic escalation still works.
4. Tests: server tests for the follow-up/resume path (`packages/server/test`), covering a second message on an ended run (no orphaned chat, transcript continuous). Add desktop component/hook tests where the chat follows the run.

\## Pointers
- `orchestrator.ts`: `sendMessage`, `requestChanges`, `wakeTask`, `wakeRun`, `continueBlockReason`
- `packages/server/src/api.ts`: run message endpoints
- `apps/desktop/src/components/sessions/SessionDetailModal.tsx` and the run chat components/hooks

Verify with `moon run root:format`, `moon run root:lint`, `moonx server:typecheck`, `moonx desktop:typecheck`, plus focused tests.

fields.title: Signed peer :subscribe is refused sig_malformed, so peer answers only arrive by polling
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
Found while filming the A2A demo (2026-10-06). Two daemons paired with `dispatch a2a pair offer/accept` (signed). When daemon A sends a question to `a2a:<peer>`, the outbound worker (packages/server/src/a2a/outbound.ts) opens `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/<id>:subscribe` on the peer. Repro: two sandbox daemons, pair them, POST /api/messages {to:['a2a:peer'],kind:'question',blocking:true}; watch the peer's log.

Acceptance:
- A signed :subscribe from a paired peer verifies and streams (no sig_malformed in the peer log).
- An answer from the peer reaches the sender's thread within a few seconds.
- A test in packages/server/test/a2a covers signed subscribe between two paired daemons.

fields.title: Overseer chat: stop yanking to the bottom; opened "details" must stay scrollable
fields.§h:Description:
\## Bug
In the Overseer chat (`apps/desktop/src/components/chat/OverseerChat.tsx`):
1. Opening a tool run's "details" and then scrolling up doesn't hold: you get pulled back to the bottom.
2. Every new message or tool call scrolls the reader all the way to the bottom, even when they have scrolled up to read.

\## Cause
The pin-to-bottom effect (~line 650, keyed on `thread.length` + `lastKey`) sets `scrollTop = scrollHeight` on every new row, whether or not the reader is at the bottom. During a turn each tool call adds a row, so any scroll-up gets undone. Also, the transcript `role="log"` is a `flex-col overflow-y-auto` whose rows can flex-shrink, so a tall expanded panel can squash the rows above it instead of making the list taller.

\## Done looks like
- New rows follow only while the reader is at or near the bottom (within ~48px). A ref updated in the log's `onScroll` is enough. Scrolling back down re-attaches.
- Sending a message (`submitDraft`) always re-attaches, so the user's own message and the reply are visible.
- Transcript rows don't shrink (`[&>*]:shrink-0` on the log), so expanding details grows the scroll height.
- The existing tests "a new transcript row re-pins to the bottom" and "a turn settling in place re-pins to the bottom" still pass.
- New test: a reader scrolled up (scrollTop 100, scrollHeight 900, clientHeight 300, fire a scroll) stays at 100 when a new row arrives.
- `root:format`, `root:lint`, `desktop:typecheck` and `desktop:test` pass. Check in the running app that opening details mid-turn stays put.

fields.title: Merge queue install fails on Intel Macs: pnpm 11.9.0 (@pnpm/exe) has no darwin-x64 binary
fields.§h:Description:
\## Bug
Every merge-queue land on this machine (Intel i9, `uname -m` = x86_64) fails at install in under a second:

```
ERR_PNPM_PNPM_ENGINE_NO_NATIVE_BINARY
Cannot run @pnpm/exe@11.9.0 on this host: it ships no native binary for darwin-x64.
help: Set `pmOnFail` to `ignore` to skip the version switch.
```

Seen on r-0f3a12, r-94fa34, r-003858, r-17e156, r-730fe5 and r-8e60a4. The pin comes from `package.json` (`"packageManager": "pnpm@11.9.0"`) and `.prototools` (`pnpm = "11.9.0"`). pnpm's version switch tries to fetch `@pnpm/exe`, which has no darwin-x64 build.

\## Done looks like
- The queue's install step works on darwin-x64. Options: pin a pnpm version whose distribution runs on darwin-x64 (keep `packageManager` and `.prototools` in sync), or have the queue's install not depend on `@pnpm/exe` for the version switch (for example `pmOnFail` / `managePackageManagerVersions`), or have the daemon run the install with the pnpm that proto already resolves.
- Pick the option that keeps CI and Apple Silicon working, and say why in the commit.
- Re-queue a finished run and confirm it lands through the merge queue on this Intel Mac.

fields.title: Close the gaps with T3 Code
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description: The five capabilities T3 Code has that fit Dispatch's task model best, from the 2026-10-09 comparison: run checkpoints and rewind, rich task input (attachments, @file mentions, window capture), ACP provider support, running agents on remote machines with mobile approvals, and scheduled or webhook-triggered tasks.

fields.title: Checkpoints and rewind for agent runs
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
T3 Code lets you 'edit from here': rewind a thread to an earlier turn and either revert the files too or keep them. Dispatch runs have no checkpoints; the only undo is discarding the worktree, send-back, or git revert.

Scope: record a checkpoint (a commit or tree snapshot in the run's worktree) at each agent turn that changed files; show them on the run page; let the user rewind a run to a checkpoint, choosing 'revert files too' or 'keep changes', then continue the run from there with a new instruction.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each turn that edited files has a checkpoint visible on the run page.
- Rewinding with 'revert files' restores the worktree exactly to that checkpoint; 'keep changes' leaves files as they are.
- A rewound run can be continued with a new message, and its transcript shows where the rewind happened.
- Works for Claude and Codex runs; tests cover checkpoint creation and both rewind modes.

fields.title: Rich task input: attachments, @file mentions and window capture
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
T3 Code accepts images, PDFs, ZIPs and video in prompts, @-mentions of files, quoting part of a reply, and a hotkey that captures a window (with its accessibility tree) into the draft. Dispatch tasks can hold attachments, but they never reach the agent, and there are no @file mentions.

Scope: pass task attachments (images, PDF, text) to the agent at dispatch and in follow-up messages; add @file mentions with fuzzy file search in the task spec, the Overseer composer and run follow-ups; add a capture-window action that attaches a screenshot to the current draft.

fields.title: Run stuck in awaiting-approval with no approval surfaced anywhere
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
\## What happened
In the audio-book project (2026-10-13), run **r-ff533a** (task t-aa7a59, executor claude, model claude-opus-5-5) showed `awaiting-approval` in `dispatch runs` for about 25 minutes. During that time:
- The desktop app's "needs me" view showed nothing waiting on the user.
- The run logged nothing after 17:44:30Z; `updatedAt` was still 2026-10-13T17:44:30.145Z.
- `dispatch run show r-ff533a --json` had no field naming the parked request. `meta` showed `lastStep: "Sub-agent: Pre-flight plan conflict scan"` and `subagents: {running: 1}`.
- The last entries were Bash tool calls made inside a sub-agent, so the parked call was probably a sub-agent's tool call.

The only fix was `dispatch cancel r-ff533a`, then `dispatch run resume r-ff533a` (which created r-95f0d8).

\## Context
- r-ff533a was itself a resume of r-d39798, made after a daemon handover. A `dispatch serve` started from a terminal took over the app's daemon and was then replaced by the app's dispatchd (pid 50497). All in-flight runs failed with "dispatchd restarted while this run was in flight" and were resumed with `dispatch run resume`.
- This may be a regression of, or an uncovered case in, t-b2d83a ("Pending scope/approval requests are lost on daemon restart and never re-surface"), specifically for resumed runs and/or approvals requested by sub-agents.

\## Expected
- A run in `awaiting-approval` always has a request the app's "needs me" view and `dispatch approvals` can see.
- If the request is lost, the run state is reconciled instead of being parked forever.
- `run show` names the pending request id and tool.

\## Acceptance
- Reproduce: resume a run after a daemon handover, then have a sub-agent hit a tool that needs approval. The request appears in the app.
- Add a watchdog or reconcile step that flags `awaiting-approval` runs with no matching pending request.
- `run show --json` exposes the pending request (tool, input summary, requestId).

fields.title: Epic status shows 'queued' with no reason when tasks are blocked by claims held by unmerged runs
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
\## What happened
In the audio-book project (2026-10-13), 7 tasks across 4 epics sat at `phase: queued` with no `REASON` in `dispatch epic status`. Epic concurrency was raised from 2 to 6 and `liveRuns` was `[]`, but nothing started for over 2 minutes. Affected tasks: t-0b1997, t-2db681, t-1f675c, t-810947, t-eff5b4, t-98dfde, t-73f4f2.

The real blocker was write claims held by runs that had **finished but were not reviewed or merged** (`phase: needs-review`):
- r-95f0d8 claims `apps/api/src/app/games/**`.
- r-46056a claims `apps/api/src/app/tts/**`.

Each queued task's `writes` overlapped one of these.

Nothing on the CLI or JSON surface said so, so it looked like a concurrency problem. I raised concurrency, which did nothing. The user also expected the app's "needs me" view to point at the reviews, but it showed nothing waiting.

\## Expected
- `epic status` (table and `--json`) gives a reason for a queued task blocked on claims, for example `waiting on claims held by r-95f0d8 (needs-review): apps/api/src/app/games/**`.
- When finished runs block queued work, the app's "needs me" view and `dispatch approvals` show "review r-… to unblock N tasks".
- Optionally: once a run has finished, narrow its claims from the declared globs to the files it actually touched. `run_list` already records both, so a broad declared glob such as `games/**` doesn't block unrelated work while the run waits for review.

\## Acceptance
- A test covers a queued child blocked by a needs-review run's claims: status reports the blocking run and its paths.
- The "needs me" view counts reviews that block queued work.

fields.title: Background dispatchd started by the app retakes the project while a terminal 'dispatch serve' has live runs, killing them
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
\## What happened
In the audio-book project (2026-10-13):
1. With the Dispatch.app daemon running (pid 39943), I ran `dispatch serve` from a terminal. It printed "Took over from the dispatchd that served this project (pid 39943, port 50522)".
2. `dispatch epic start` on 8 epics started 7 runs on the terminal daemon.
3. A few minutes later the app started a new background dispatchd (`/Applications/Dispatch.app/.../dispatchd --root … --idle-timeout`, pid 50497). It took the project back, and the terminal `dispatch serve` exited with code 0 and no message.
4. All 7 in-flight runs went `failed` with "dispatchd restarted while this run was in flight; the agent process may still be running". They had to be resumed one at a time with `dispatch run resume`.

The help text for `approvals` says a terminal `dispatch serve` "takes over the background daemon (once it has no live work)". The reverse direction, the app's background daemon taking over from a terminal daemon, does not appear to wait for live work.

\## Expected
- No takeover, in either direction, while the current daemon has live runs. Either wait for the runs to finish or hand them over.
- If a takeover happens anyway, in-flight runs are adopted or resumed automatically instead of being failed.
- The terminal `dispatch serve` prints why it exited.

\## Acceptance
- Reproduce: start runs under a terminal `dispatch serve`, then trigger the app's background daemon. Runs survive or are auto-resumed, and the terminal daemon logs the takeover reason.

fields.title: Epic never re-dispatches a task whose last run was cancelled (stuck 'queued', no reason)
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
Repro (audio-book project, epic e-fbe7ce, concurrency 6, no spend cap):
1. Task F1 (t-bfcff9) blockedBy F0. F0 was set landed, so the epic dispatched F1 as run r-13f1a7.
2. F0 was set back to ready and r-13f1a7 was cancelled; F1's status went back to draft.
3. Later F0 was set landed again and F1 set to ready.

Expected: the epic dispatches F1 again on its next tick.
Actual: dispatch epic status shows F1 phase=queued, status=ready, with an empty REASON column, for ~2 days. The daemon (Dispatch.app background dispatchd) was running, there were no live runs, and no other task held a write claim. 'dispatch run t-bfcff9 --fresh' started it immediately (r-164052), so nothing actually blocked it.

Likely cause: the epic treats a task with a prior (cancelled) run as already dispatched. Either re-dispatch after cancellation when the task is ready again, or show a REASON (e.g. 'last run cancelled; run dispatch run <task> --fresh').

fields.title: Keep the computer awake while agents are working
fields.creator: agent:local-cli

Claude Desktop added "Keep computer awake" (v1.46388.1 / v1.52386.0): a setting, plus a per-session menu item, that blocks idle sleep while Claude works. Dispatch has nothing like it. fields.title: Usage limit: hold messages and resume runs automatically when the limit resets
fields.creator: agent:local-cli
fields.§h:Description:
Claude Desktop v1.46388.1, v1.49585.0 and v2.19675.0: messages sent after the 5-hour limit is hit wait above the composer and go out automatically when the limit resets. v2.37337.1 also made background agents continue after the reset.

**Build**

- Messages sent to a parked run or the Overseer are held, shown as queued with "Sends when your limit resets at 3:40 PM", and delivered on resume. Reuse the queue from t-d5e0d3 if it has landed.

**Acceptance**
